name: Accordion
summary: A stack of questions or sections that open one at a time, built on native details elements.
description: Use it for FAQs and long settings pages where people only need one answer at a time. Give every item the same name to make the group exclusive; leave the name out to let several open at once. Do not hide content that most people need to read.

classes.name: v-accordion
classes.description: The group. Put <details> items with a <summary> inside; it draws the dividers and the chevron.

states.description: On a <details>: the item is open and its chevron points up in the accent colour.
The same name on every <details> makes the group exclusive: opening one closes the others. Browsers without support let items open independently.

keyboard.action: Moves focus between the item headers.
Opens or closes the focused item.

a11y: The <summary> is the button: browsers expose it with its expanded state, so no ARIA is needed.
Keep the summary text short and specific, it is all a screen reader hears before opening.
The height animation runs only where ::details-content is supported and is off with reduced motion.
Content inside a closed item is still found by the browser find-in-page, which opens the item.

examples.title: Exclusive FAQ
examples.description: All items share name="faq", so one opens at a time.
examples.html:
Do I need JavaScript for this?

No. The accordion is native details elements sharing one name, so opening one closes the others.

Can several items be open at once?

Leave out the name attribute and every item opens on its own.

Does it animate?

Where the browser supports it, the height eases open. With reduced motion it opens at once.

examples.title: Independent items
examples.description: Without a name, each item opens and closes on its own.
